record_type_quote: Here, I sought to replicate both the within and between-subjects’ effects of confidence judgments on thought probe validity.

targets.authors: Seli, Jonker, Cheyne, Cortes, and Smilek
targets.evidence_quote: Here, I sought to replicate both the within and between-subjects’ effects of confidence judgments on thought probe validity.
targets.outcome_quote: Although I found no evidence for individual differences in thought report validity and only very weak evidence for individual differences in thought monitoring, I did find support for two other findings that Seli et al. described as key: 1) Variation in the confidence ratings that subjects provide with the distributions of confidence reports being remarkably similar to those found in Seli et al. (see Table 4 for comparisons across studies and administrations); 2) Some support for the within-subjects’ finding that when subjects reported low confidence, response time variability did not significantly differ between reports of on-task and mind-wandering.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly contrast absent individual differences with support for two other key original findings. Weak within-subject support is described as limited to the first administration. The conclusion questions the broad original assertion but does not label the whole replication uniformly failed.

reasoning: One published paper is explicitly re-tested with 291 new participants. The manuscript reference list omits the specific five-author 2015 target despite repeated citations, so the title and DOI are left empty; author names and year occur in the abstract. Other cited mind-wandering papers provide background or validation rather than independent target studies.
